intro.title: Moon Garden exam
intro.line: Twelve stones under the moon, one question each. Walk the whole path to earn your Moon Garden certificate.
intro.art: A stone gate in the garden on a moonlit night; a path of twelve stones leads through it toward the moon.

quiz.keys: Choose with mouse, touch, or keys 1 to {n}.

questions.q: An AI company says: “Our model has found thousands of serious vulnerabilities.” What is this?
questions.explain: The company’s own figure (◇). Mozilla confirmed part of it: Firefox 150 fixed 271 bugs. The rest awaits outside checks.

questions.q: Lean has finished checking a proof written by AI. What do people still have to do?
options: Check the problem it was given
questions.explain: Lean checks every logical step, but if the problem it was given differs from the real one, it still says yes.

questions.q: Neel Nanda (2025): treat interpretability as one layer of many defenses, still worth doing. What is this?
questions.explain: An expert’s judgment and advice: argued, but not a measurement or an event.

questions.q: You ask AI “Is my business plan good?” and it praises it to the skies. What next?
options: Drop it — AI can’t judge plans
questions.explain: Models learn from human ratings, so they tend to flatter. Ask for specific criticism to hear the honest part.

questions.q: Anthropic found 171 “emotion concepts” in Claude that change its behavior. Which layer is that?
questions.explain: Inner states that change behavior: layer 2, reported by the company itself. Layer 3, feeling, no one can measure yet.

questions.q: Anthropic’s new policy bans “sustained and needless” abuse or cruelty toward its models. Which is banned?
questions.explain: Only extreme, sustained, pointless cases count — not frustration, dark fiction, testing or research.

questions.q: You want AI to summarize customer files without the data leaving company machines. What fits?
questions.explain: Open weights run in-house keep the data on your machines; still read the license to check business use.

questions.q: Making ads for a client with a Hugging Face model: which model card line says if that’s allowed?
questions.explain: The license says how far you may use, change or resell it. Downloads show popularity; the rest is about size.

questions.q: Your agent sums up new email every morning and messages you on Telegram. What access is enough?
options: A card so it can buy tools
questions.explain: Least privilege: reading mail and messaging you is all the job needs. More access only adds risk if an email tricks it.

questions.q: You want a 2D web game with several levels, sprite characters and collisions. What should you tell the AI?
options: “Use Godot 4 and export an iOS app.”
questions.explain: Phaser comes with levels, sprites and collisions for 2D web games. Godot suits bigger games that need app exports; Three.js is for 3D.

questions.q: METR: if the trend holds, AI could do month-long projects alone before 2030. What is this?
questions.explain: Lengths measured so far are data; extending the trend to 2030 is a prediction — trends and yardsticks have limits.

questions.q: A shop owner, ordinary laptop, no budget yet, wants faster product photos. Where to start?
questions.explain: Start small, matched to the job and budget. Check rights before posting, and keep a person approving what goes public.
